name: WASP-84
description: Star of 5,300 K, 101 parsecs away, with 1 transiting planet.

radius.source: Maciejewski et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-84 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive

mass.source: Maciejewski et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-84 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive

temperature.source: Bonomo et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of WASP-84 b's parameter set from Bonomo et al. 2017 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive

text.card: WASP-84 b crosses WASP-84 as seen from Earth, which is how it was found.
text.introduction: Its radius follows Maciejewski et al. 2023, and its temperature Bonomo et al. 2017.
text.locator: NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (st_refname BONOMO_ET_AL__2017, MACIEJEWSKI_ET_AL_2023): st_teff 5300, st_rad 0.768, st_mass 0.853

quotes.title: WASP-84
quotes.card: WASP-84, also known as BD+02 2056, is a G-type main-sequence star 327 light-years away in the constellation Hydra.
quotes.introduction: Its surface temperature is 5350±31 K and is slightly enriched in heavy elements compared to the Sun, with a metallicity Fe/H index of 0.05±0.02.

notes: WASP-84 c: Maciejewski et al. 2023's mass 0.048 Jupiter masses in 0.174 Jupiter radii is 11.3 g/cm^3, outside what the records accept
